races.title: State Senate, District 7
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Michael Lee
cands.bio: Wilmington attorney who founded his own law firm. Republican state senator, elected in 2014 to District 9 and serving 2014–2019, then again from 2021, now in District 7. Senate Majority Leader since 2025. UNC-Chapel Hill and Wake Forest Law graduate.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Michael Lee was born, where he grew up, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no stated position or action on data centers, homestead or property-tax elimination, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, or gun laws. His campaign site's claims about income-tax and teacher-pay votes are his own statements, not confirmed records. The Ballotpedia page listed no endorsements for 2026. The campaign site pages were cut off partway, so some priorities text was not read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney who founded his own firm. State senator for District 9 (2014–2019, 2021–2022) and District 7 (2023 on), Senate Majority Leader since 2025. Has chaired the Education/Higher Education committee and, per his campaign site, the Appropriations/Base Budget committee.
qual.why: Long prior legislative service, chamber leadership as Majority Leader, and a law career fit the highest band for writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Long prior legislative service, chamber leadership as Majority Leader, and a law career fit the highest band for writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he voted for every teacher pay raise since 2014, including the newest budget's average 8% increase and $48,000 starting pay. It also says he supports options for families when a child's needs aren't being met. This is the campaign's own account and I did not verify it against roll calls.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he supports law enforcement, first responders, school safety and clear consequences for violent crime.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Jessica Bichler
cands.bio: Wilmington small business owner and yoga teacher who co-owns a yoga studio. Began her career in the film industry as a production coordinator. A Democrat, she defeated incumbent Senate Majority Leader Michael Lee in 2026 for N.C. Senate District 7, her first run for office.

endorsements.text: Her Ballotpedia survey response lists endorsements from Vote Save America, Vote Mama, The First Ask, States Win, Electing Women Alliance, EMILY's List and Lillian's List (self-reported). Ballotpedia also lists several Sway voting-group recommendations.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jessica Bichler was born or raised, or any exact date she moved to North Carolina beyond "almost 15 years" in Wilmington. She has never held office, so there are no past votes or official actions to report. We found no news coverage of controversies, no stated position on land-buying by foreign or institutional investors, immigration or H-1B, and no pledge on refusing particular kinds of donations. Her only data center statement is a call to regulate them to protect ratepayers.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign says she has lived in Wilmington for almost 15 years, which puts her arrival as an adult in the 10-25 year range; her birthplace and where she grew up are not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Co-owns a yoga studio in Wilmington and has taught yoga for over a decade; earlier worked in the film industry as a production coordinator. She has held no prior elected office.
qual.why: A business owner with no legislative, policy or budget career and no prior office, which places her in the middle range for the business-owner category.
qual.label: A business owner with no legislative, policy or budget career and no prior office, which places her in the middle range for the business-owner category.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says homeowners, seniors and people on fixed incomes should be able to stay in their communities without being pushed out by high taxes, and lists "lower taxes for working families and the middle class" and protecting homeowners from being priced out as goals. She does not propose eliminating homestead taxes or cutting local spending.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Lists "support sustainable growth in our region" as a priority and says she wants to protect the county's water, air and beaches.

back-police-order.evidence: Says the state must give local law enforcement the resources to fill vacancies, train recruits and respond to emergencies, and lists "invest in local law enforcement and first responders" as a goal.

second-amendment.evidence: Says she wants "common-sense gun safety measures, like background checks" while respecting responsible ownership under the 2nd Amendment.

pro-life.evidence: Says she wants to restore reproductive rights and prevent further bans on reproductive care, including abortion and contraception access.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

roots.summary: Her campaign says she has lived in Wilmington for almost 15 years, which puts her arrival as an adult in the 10-25 year range; her birthplace and where she grew up are not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Her campaign site says data centers use large amounts of energy and water and that utility costs are rising as providers shift the financial burden of new data centers onto community members. She calls for regulating data center infrastructure to avoid higher energy costs for ratepayers. She does not call for a ban or moratorium.
